statements.text: 1 (Local Non-triviality (LNT)). Given a dataset 𝐷 with joint probability distribution 𝑃𝐷 and a statement sketch 𝑠 [·], we say that 𝑠 [·] is locally non-trivial (LNT) if and only if 𝑎 𝑗 ⫫∕ 𝑎 𝒌 , where 𝑎 𝑗 is the dependent attribute in the ON clause, 𝑎 𝒌 is the determinant set of 𝑎 𝑗 in the GIVEN clause, and ⫫∕ denotes statistical dependence. A program sketch 𝑝 [·] is said to be LNT if and only if all statement sketches in 𝑝 [·] are LNT. Def. 4.1 regulates the notion of validity of statement sketches. Recall that the sketch encodes the inter-variable dependencies of a program. In particular, it enforces that the statement sketches must entail a statistical correlation between the dependent attribute and the determinant set. LNT implies that there exists a concretized statement 𝑠 [𝑏 + ] that is at least better than a random guess. For example, in the dataset described in Example 3.1, the statement sketch 𝑠 [·] = GIVEN PostalCode ON City is LNT because PostalCode and City are statistically correlated.

Given a dataset 𝐷 with its joint probability distribution 𝑃𝐷 and a PGM 𝐺, if 𝑃𝐷 is Markovian to 𝐺, for a variable 𝑎𝑖 and its parent variables 𝑎 𝒌 in 𝐺, the statement sketch 𝑠 [·] with the determinant set of 𝑎 𝒌 and the dependent attribute 𝑎𝑖 is LNT. Therefore, the above proposition implies that, when the structure of the PGM is available, one can effortlessly extract a LNT program sketch according to the above proposition. In the following theorem, we further enhance the claim and show that a PGM inherently entail a GNT program sketch.
Given a dataset 𝐷 with its underlying joint probability distribution 𝑃𝐷 and a PGM 𝐺, if 𝑃𝐷 is faithful to 𝐺, then the program sketch 𝑝 [·] that is derived from 𝐺 is GNT.

1 allows us to directly derive a GNT program sketch from PGM. However, the full structure of PGM is not practically learnable from the data. Next, we show that the MECs can be used to partially deduce a GNT program sketch. 4.4 Characterizing Practically Learnable Sketches from MECs Due to the limitations of the existing structure learning algorithms, the full structure of the PGM is not practically learnable from the data. In this section, we aim to understand under what conditions we can still (partially) deduce a GNT program sketch in practice. Given the identifiability issue of the PGM [38], we cannot uniquely identify the PGM from the data distribution in general. Instead, Proc. ACM Manag. Data, Vol. 3, No. 4 (SIGMOD), Article 248. Compared to the original DAG, the MEC is a summary of multiple possible DAGs given the data, which is defined as follows.

Given a LNT statement sketch 𝑠 [·] from a MEC [𝐺], with determinant set 𝑎 𝒌 and dependent attribute 𝑎 𝑗 , if 𝑎 𝑗 is adjacent to every attribute in 𝑎 𝒌 and each attribute in 𝑎 𝒌 is non-adjacent to the others, then in every 𝐺 of [𝐺], there is a directed edge from each attribute in 𝑎 𝒌 to 𝑎 𝑗 . And, no other directed edges exist to 𝑎 𝑗 in every 𝐺 of [𝐺].

Consider two conjunctive LNT statement sketches 𝑠 1 [·], 𝑠 2 [·]. Let 𝑎 1𝒌 and 𝑎 2𝒌 = {𝑎𝑖 } be the determinant set and 𝑎𝑖 and 𝑎 𝑗 the dependent attributes for 𝑠 1 [·] and 𝑠 2 [·], respectively. Then, in every 𝐺 of [𝐺], there is a directed edge from 𝑎𝑖 to 𝑎 𝑗 , and no other directed edges to 𝑎 𝑗 .

Consider two conjunctive LNT statement sketches 𝑠 2 [·], 𝑠 3 [·]. Let 𝑎 2𝒌 = {𝑎𝑖 } and 3 𝑎 𝒌 = {𝑎 𝑗 } be the determinant set and 𝑎 𝑗 and 𝑎𝑙 the dependent attributes for 𝑠 2 [·] and 𝑠 3 [·], respectively. If 𝑠 2 [·] satisfies Proposition 2, then in every 𝐺 of the MEC [𝐺], there is a directed edge from 𝑎 𝑗 to 𝑎𝑙 , and no other directed edges to 𝑎𝑙 . We prove Proposition 2 above and both Proposition 3 and 4 are direct corollary of Proposition 2. We present a visual interpretation of these propositions in Fig. 5. Intuitively, Proposition 2 states that when a statement sketch 𝑠 [·] has more than one determinant attribute, it is unique in the MEC and can be directly extracted. Proposition 3 and 4 further claims that all its descendant statement sketches can be uniquely identified in the MEC. proofs.text: Without loss of generality, let 𝑠 [·] be an arbitrary statement sketch in 𝑝 [·]. In the context of the PGM, 𝑠 [·] corresponds to one or a few directed edges from 𝑎 𝒌 to 𝑎 𝑗 in 𝐺, where 𝑎 𝒌 is the determinant attributes and 𝑎 𝑗 is the dependent attribute in 𝑠 [·]. By Proposition 1, 𝑠 [·] is locally non-trivial. Therefore, we have that 𝑎 𝑗 ⫫∕ 𝑎 𝒌 . To show that 𝑠 [·] is globally non-trivial, we need to show that 𝑎 𝑗 ⫫∕ 𝑎 𝒌 on any subset of the data that is conditioned on other statement sketches in 𝑝 [·] (i.e., 𝐷 𝑏 where 𝑏 is a condition on other statement sketches in 𝑝 [·]). That is, the above condition is equivalent to showing that 𝑎 𝑗 ⫫∕ 𝑎 𝒌 | 𝑏, where 𝑏 is the condition. Since we are to show that 𝑎 𝑗 ⫫∕ 𝑎 𝒌 on any possible 𝑏, we can further rewrite the condition as 𝑎 𝑗 ⫫∕ 𝑎 𝒌 | 𝑎 𝒛 where 𝑎 𝒛 is any set of determinant attributes that are comprised by 𝑝 [·]. Since 𝑃𝐷 is faithful to 𝐺, we have that 𝑎 𝑗 ⫫∕ 𝑎 𝒌 | 𝑎 𝒛 for any 𝑎 𝒛 . Therefore, we have that 𝑠 [·] is globally non-trivial. □

We first prove the presence of directed edges from each attribute in 𝑎 𝒌 to 𝑎 𝑗 in every DAG 𝐺 within the MEC [𝐺] by contradiction. Assume that for some pair of attributes 𝑎𝑙 , 𝑎𝑚 ∈ 𝑎 𝒌 , the triplet 𝑎𝑙 , 𝑎 𝑗 , 𝑎𝑚 does not form a v-structure in [𝐺]. This means that we do not have the configuration 𝑎𝑙 → 𝑎 𝑗 ← 𝑎𝑚 . According to the definition of faithfulness, the absence of a v-structure implies that for any set of attributes 𝑎 𝒛 ⊂ 𝐷 that renders 𝑎𝑙 and 𝑎𝑚 conditionally independent, 𝑎 𝑗 must not be in 𝑎 𝒛 . However, by the definition of a locally non-trivial statement sketch, we have that 𝑎𝑙 is not conditionally independent of 𝑎𝑚 given 𝑎 𝑗 , denoted as 𝑎𝑙 ⫫∕ 𝑎𝑚 | 𝑎 𝑗 . This is a contradiction to the assumption that 𝑎𝑙 , 𝑎 𝑗 , 𝑎𝑚 do not form a v-structure, as the presence of 𝑎 𝑗 in the conditioning set should not affect the conditional independence of 𝑎𝑙 and 𝑎𝑚 if they do not form a v-structure. Therefore, the only consistent configuration under the MEC [𝐺] is that 𝑎𝑙 , 𝑎 𝑗 , 𝑎𝑚 must form a v-structure, which implies that there is a directed edge from 𝑎𝑙 to 𝑎 𝑗 and from 𝑎𝑚 to 𝑎 𝑗 in every DAG 𝐺 within the MEC [𝐺]. Then, we prove the absence of other directed edges to 𝑎 𝑗 in every DAG 𝐺 within the MEC [𝐺] by contradiction. Assume that there exists a directed edge from 𝑎𝑞 ∉ 𝑎 𝒌 to 𝑎 𝑗 in some DAG 𝐺 within the MEC [𝐺]. 𝑎𝑞 → 𝑎 𝑗 ← 𝑎𝑚 (where 𝑎𝑚 ∈ 𝑎 𝒌 ) forms a v-structure in 𝐺. This implies that 𝑎𝑞 ⫫∕ 𝑎𝑚 | 𝑎 𝑗 . However, by the definition of statement sketch, it is clear that 𝑎 𝒌 are the only determinant set of 𝑎 𝑗 . Therefore, the dependency between 𝑎𝑞 and 𝑎𝑚 must be mediated by 𝑎 𝑗 . That is, 𝑎𝑞 ⫫ 𝑎𝑚 | 𝑎 𝑗 . This is a contradiction to 𝑎𝑞 ⫫∕ 𝑎𝑚 | 𝑎 𝑗 . □
